Definition
In this lesson, you will use an encoder wheel position sensor to determine position.
INTRODUCTIONM
As an optional part of the lesson, you will use an increment wheel position sensor to determine position.
These methods of position sensing are very common.

The resolution of the wheel is 22.5 degrees per mark. Note that the resolution of the encoder is also 22.5. Where 2 to the N power equals 16 because there are four tracks (not counting the strobe track).
Of course, the encoder and increment position sensors are digital.

ENCODER POSITION SENSOR
In this experiment, you will observe the operation of an encoder wheel sensor and determine its position.
EXPERIMENT
This position sensor is manually operated, you will act as the prime mover.
Pick up the PC130-256 card and examine it..................
Locate the wheel. Notice that it has 16 positions, 0 through F. These numbers are for you to visually determine position.
Look underneath the wheel on the left hand side. You should be able to see the sensors.
You should also be able to see light and dark areas around the wheel on the reverse side.
These areas absorb or reflect light and represent the code.
Locate the IC's on the card during the following description. To view the schematic, select the schematic button.
There are five photosensors on the card, four for each number track and one for the strobe track, PS1 through PS5. The sensors are located underneath the wheel on the left hand side.
The outputs of the five photosensors are shaped by the schmitt triggers in the inverters of IC2. IC2 is located underneath the wheel towards the bottom of the card.
The four outputs form the number tracks are first applied to IC1, a seven segment LED driver. IC1 is located in the upper center of the card.
The output of the driver is applied to DS1, a seven segment LED. The LED will indicate the position of the wheel. DS1 is located in the upper right of the card.
The outputs (all five) of the inverters are also applied to IC3, a latch. IC3 is located in the lower right of the card.
The latch is enabled by the strobe pulse. This means that on each strobe, the data from the number tracks will be latched into Q0 through Q3 outputs.
The outputs of the latch, which are delayed by one position, are applied to the A inputs of IC4, a comparator IC. IC4 is located beneath the wheel on the right hand side.
The B inputs to IC4 are the outputs of the four number tracks directly.
IC4 then compares the two inputs, the current position and the old position. The output of the comparator indicates if the wheel is turning clockwise (A>B) or counter clockwise (A<B).
The result of the comparison is indicated by LEDs DS2 (red) or DS3 (green) through IC5, and an amplifier. IC5 is located just below DS2 and DS3.
Being able to detect the direction, of motion is one advantage the encoder wheel has over the increment wheel. An increment wheel has no method of determining direction since only marks are counted..
